Letter to Parents from Rowhill Governors - 04/01/24

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Rowhill School
Creating opportunities for a brighter future
Rowhill is a pupil referral unit based in North East Hampshire serving 13 mainstream secondary schools. Students are referred to our school if they are medically unwell or emotionally vulnerable, at risk of permanent exclusion or have been permanently excluded from their mainstream school. We specialise in providing tailored educational support to help our students overcome challenges which have meant they have struggled in their mainstream school.
At Rowhill School, we strive to create a nurturing environment where ambition meets compassion, ensuring that every member of our school community feels included and valued. We are committed to delivering a flexible curriculum that is designed to challenge and inspire our students. We believe in the power of education to transform lives. Our aim is to prepare our students not only for academic success but also to develop the attributes, skills and knowledge they need to successfully navigate their future pathways in our modern world.
Every interaction is a learning experience and every learning experience must be an opportunity for progress
Our curriculum is designed to ensure that students are being taught from the moment that they interact with a member of our staff team. We not only focus on the knowledge that they need to obtain qualification but also the attributes and skills they need to be successfully navigate through their future. Our approach is based on relational and restorative practice and our school week is designed to provide opportunities for students and staff to build effective relationships alongside ensuring students have access to a range of ambitious learning opportunities.
We hope that you enjoy exploring our website. Please do not hesitate to contact us should you wish to know more about our school.
Vicky Essex (Executive Head Teacher) Laura Hann (Head of School)

Learning Vision
"Every interaction will be a learning experience, and every learning experience must be an opportunity for progress."Our curriculum is designed to ensure that the Attributes, Skills and Knowledge that a young person needs is explicitly taught to them rather than left to chance.
Nurture
We strive to create a nurturing environment where ambition meets compassion, ensuring that every member of our school community feels included and valued.
Flexible Curriculum
We are committed to delivering a flexible curriculum that is designed to challenge and inspire our students. We believe in the power of education to transform lives.
Prepare
Our aim is to prepare our students not only for academic success but also to develop the attributes, skills and knowledge they need to successfully navigate their future pathways in our modern world.
Please download our Learning Vision Booklet here!

At Rowhill School, we strive to create a nurturing environment where ambition meets compassion, ensuring that every member of our school community feels included and valued.

Our aim is to prepare our students not only for academic success but also to develop the attributes, skills and knowledge they need to successfully navigate their future pathways in our modern world.

Pupil Premium
The Pupil Premium is money allocated to the school by the Government to support students who are eligible for Free School Meals, are in the Care of the Local Authority, have been Adopted from Care or are from Service Families.
The amount that the school receives for each student varies depending on which category that they are in.
It is the school’s decision how to use this funding in the best interests of these students to:
raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils and close the attainment gap with their peers
support children and young people with parents in the regular armed forces

Curriculum
At Key Stage 4 (KS4), students follow a core curriculum of English Language, Maths, Science, PE and PSHE/PD alongside subjects such as Humanities, Art, and Hospitality & Catering.
At Key Stage 3 (KS3), students study English, Maths, Science, PE, PSHE/PDL, Art and Hospitality & Catering.
For further details about our curriculum, please contact Head of School, Laura Hann or our Curriculum Leads Richard Moger & Simon Hutchison.
English Language
Qualifications associated with it including how they are assessed.
GCSE English Language (AQA) - 2 Externally set papers sat in May/June.
Functional skills English (Edexcel) - 2 externally set papers (reading and writing)sat in November and March, Speaking and listening completed internally under controlled conditions.
A brief overview of what the pupils will be learning in each year group.
Year 11 - Will be working on the essential English skills for lifelong learning. These include reading fiction, descriptive writing, analysis of text and writing to argue and explain.
Year 10 - Will be looking at developing their English skills from KS3 looking at a wide range of texts and skills. This will include different ways of writing, analysis of texts, reading fiction and non fiction.
KS3 - Will be looking at a wide variety of themes and text throughout the academic year. They will look at non-fiction writing, a Victorian Christmas, dystopian and post 1914 literature as well as poetry and creative writing. In addition there will be opportunities to write in different forms as well.
Maths
Qualifications associated with it including how they are assessed.
GCSE Maths(AQA) - 3 papers - all sat in May/June.
Functional Skills Maths (Edexcel) - 2 papers sat at determined points in the school year
A brief overview of what the pupils will be learning in each year group.
Year 11 - An interleaving approach takes place looking to overlap different concepts and fill in gaps in pupils knowledge and skills. After each set of mocks/Functional skills exam in the academic year, lessons will be adapted to support pupil need based on areas for development.
Year 10 - Will cover the key foundation topics in maths that will be taught to mastery so that they have a secure understanding that can be built on throughout KS4. This will include; number, algebra, geometry and proportional reasoning.
KS3 - Will cover the key skills toolkit at the start of the year with the aim of equipping pupils with the knowledge and skills that will prepare them for a return to mainstream school. Lessons will be taught to age related expectations of the individual pupils and adapted according to the needs of the pupil.

Remote Education
Pupils will be directed to remote learning either as part of our Rowhill Refresh Programme or as part of a provision where pupils are moving from a full-time off-site learning programme, to an on site one. The remote learning will form part of their reintegration back onto the school site.
Academy 21
Our preferred online learning provider is Academy21 covering a broad range of core and non-sore subjects.
Lessons are in real time with the option of consolidation and/or recorded sessions if required. In addition to this essential study skills and tutorials are encouraged.
Students can interact with their teacher, and lesson content through polling tools, quizzes, written responses in chat pods, on mic or through whiteboards. They can also communicate directly with the teacher in a private chat pod if they feel more comfortable to do so.
There is daily reporting on student's effort, understanding, and engagement. These scores enable our teachers to identify areas where students may need more support and tailor their teaching methods accordingly. Students' schools can access teacher feedback and regular reports via their Mentor Portal to easily view the student's progress.
You can find out more about Academy 21 here on their website.

Admissions
The Local Authority has the statutory duty to commission education for pupils who have been permanently excluded and those who have been diagnosed as being too emotionally vulnerable or unwell to attend school.
There is no requirement for this provision to be made at Education Centres however, Hampshire County Council commissions places at Education Centres for these pupils.

Enrichment
Our Enrichment Programme is designed to support our pupils’ individual needs and forms the foundation of our school’s relational practice.
This approach is woven into every aspect of the Enrichment Programme. Staff will continue to develop strong, empathetic connections with pupils, ensuring that every interaction reinforces positive relationships.
These relationships are the cornerstone of our strategy for helping pupils with social, emotional, and mental health (S.E.M.H.) needs to feel understood, valued, and supported, which in turn fosters greater emotional regulation, social engagement, and academic success.
The programme provides a structured yet flexible environment where students can thrive through tailored activities that promote well-being and positive behaviour, reinforcing the school’s commitment to nurturing supportive, respectful, and caring relationships.
To learn more about our vision and future of the programme please download and read the pdf file here.
Should you wish to contact us regarding our enrichment programme, please contact Marianna Morey, Enrichment Lead via email at m.morey@rowhill.hants.sch.uk

At Rowhill School, we consider the safeguarding of our children as the highest priority and work closely with our mainstream partners and local community to keep our pupils safe.

Please note that these contact details are not manned 24/7. If you have immediate concerns you should contact the police on 999.
If you have concern for a child that is not immediate, the Children’s Reception Team can be contacted on 0300 555 1384 and referrals can be made via the Inter-Agency Referral Form.
Staff Training
All staff are trained according to statutory guidance and take part in consistent refresher training throughout the year. We recognise that every single member of staff has a key role in keeping our pupil’s safe.
We also have staff that specialise in a number of topics including Mental Health and Child Criminal Exploitation to ensure that all pupil’s get the support that is right for them.
Safeguarding Curriculum
We have a responsive safeguarding curriculum that reflects the needs of our current cohort and involves us working closely with our local community. Our curriculum is regularly reviewed and updated to reflect any adaptations that are required.
Online Safety
Online Safety is one of our key safeguarding themes and we work in partnership with National Online Safety to support our staff, pupils and parents.
